newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Metals drag Australia stocks down, ignores Wall St.
newsitem.headline: Metals drag Australia stocks down, ignores Wall St.

text.p: The Australian share market was dragged to a lower close on Tuesday by a weak resource sector, which was hit by lower metal prices and ignored the record high hit on Wall Street on Monday.
The All Ordinaries index was 13.4 points down at 2,254.4, just off the low of 2,252.9. The fall almost wiped out the previous day's 15.5 point gain.
The September share price index futures was 10 points down at 2262, increasing its premium slightly to the underlying index to 7.6 points.

One Sydney-based broker said a large portfolio trade worth around A$100 million (US$78.9 million) was put through the market in morning trade in response to Monday's Wall Street rally, putting a cap on the market.
"There have also been lots of negative comments coming out of management and economic commentators lately, which means things aren't so rosy as they were a few months ago," the broker said.
Earlier, retailer David Jones said trading for the next 12 months would be difficult, after the group reported a year profit short of its prospectus forecasts made late in 1995.
"Plus metal prices are near their cyclical lows and if you put all that together it makes our market quite a unique animal," the Sydney broker said.
Most of the falls were amongst resources, while many industrial indices chalked up small rises.
Falls outnumbered rises by almost a third.
Market bellwether BHP retested the A$16.00 level, weighed down by soft copper prices and nervousness ahead of its first quarter results on Friday.
